overall_strategy: Because Mario is a young (3-month) Golden Retriever living in an apartment with no yard and a beef allergy, the plan balances immediate setup essentials (cooling mat, safe confinement, harness/leash, bedding) with a strong focus on consumables you’ll use up predictably while housetraining: full-size large-breed puppy kibble on autoship (~6-week cadence), supplemental wet food, training treats, potty pads (small and bulk), and poop bags timed to typical puppy walk frequency. Include grooming and dental supplies on a quarterly cadence to build long-term routines, and pheromone refills monthly during noise/stress periods. One-time durable buys prioritize safety, comfort, and enrichment (playpen/crate mattress, slow-feeder, leash/harness, grooming tools, camera) so you aren’t reordering long-lived items. I tuned estimated frequencies using Mario’s weight (30 lb), age (3 months), low activity (lower calorie burn but still frequent potty needs), light chew strength (so fewer toy replacements), and apartment constraints (no yard → higher pad/bag use). This approach minimizes waste, keeps Mario comfortable through training and seasonal heat, and automates the consumables you’ll reliably need most.
